## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates significant Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 186 matching segments shared across 32 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual overlaps occur with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the two volumes of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Substantial shared segments, particularly formulaic spans in verses §13–18, are also distributed among numerous other poems in the *Therāpadāna* and *Therīapadāna*, including the *Kisāgotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 22), *Soṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 26), *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20), *Nandātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 25), and *Sīvalittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 545) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically detects alignments between the text and several non-Pali sources, notably twelve matching passages with the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2), ten matches with Kṣemendra's Sanskrit *Sumāgadhāvadāna*, and five matches with the Tibetan translation of the *Lalitavistara* (D0095) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
